subject: Invoice 2027-08-INV-4321 — clarification on decimal rounding and per-request attribution
messages:
From: Olivia Park <olivia@brightcart.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Sep 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice 2027-08-INV-4321 — small but persistent rounding/skew question

Hi Ben,

Quick one on invoice INV-4321 (August usage). Our AP noticed a small recurring discrepancy between the per-request token sums we compute and the invoice line for 'generation tokens' — about 0.4% higher on your side. It's small in absolute, but it persists month-over-month and pushes VAT by a non-trivial amount for our EU entity.

We'd like:
- A short explanation of whether Redwood rounds token counts per request, per-session, or at the aggregate ledger level for invoices.
- The raw usage export (CSV) for our tenant for August and any sampling rules applied.
- If you do per-request rounding, can you show a quick reconciliation that demonstrates how the 0.4% emerges?

I've attached our AP note and the invoice PDF. Happy to hop on a quick 20-minute call if that helps.

Thanks —
Olivia Park
Finance Manager, BrightCart

Attachments: BrightCart-AP-note.pdf, 202708-invoice-INV-4321.pdf

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@brightcart.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice 2027-08-INV-4321 — small but persistent rounding/skew question

Hi Olivia — thanks for flagging and for the clear note. We've seen this pattern before with a subset of customers where fractional token attribution per request (vs. post-aggregation rounding) causes a tiny upward bias once VAT/pricing is applied.

Immediate next steps from our side:
1) I'll pull the full tenant usage export (per-request granularity) for August and include the rounding flags.
2) David — can you run the per-request vs ledger-aggregate reconciliation for tenant brightcart (sample at 1,000 requests + full CSV) and attach the CSV?
3) We'll propose a provisional credit if the delta is material after we verify.

I'll aim to get the export and a preliminary reconciliation back to you by EOD Wednesday. If AP wants a formal statement for their VAT team we'll provide the math.

Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0122

Attachments: none

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice 2027-08-INV-4321 — small but persistent rounding/skew question

Looping in Neha for tax/VAT angle (she's handled BrightCart before). David — when you run the reconciliation, please include both: (a) per-request rounding (round tokens to nearest integer before summing) and (b) ledger-level rounding (sum fractional tokens then round once). Also include sequence-length buckets — the bias tends to show up more in lots of short requests.

If the delta is within 0.5% we can offer a goodwill credit rather than a contract amendment, but we should quantify the VAT impact to BrightCart's EU entity.

Thanks,
Lauren

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@brightcart.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice 2027-08-INV-4321 — reconciliation export attached

Olivia — attaching the exports and a short reconciliation summary.

What I ran: 1, full per-request export (usage-export-202708-tenant-brightcart.csv), 2, an aggregated ledger file (summed fractions then rounded), 3, a 1,000-request sample (sample-requests-202708.json) where I demonstrate the step-by-step arithmetic.

Short findings:
- Per-request rounding (round tokens per call) produces +0.34% token count vs aggregate-rounding for August (BrightCart's profile is heavy on short conversational calls with avg tokens/request 18).
- The difference arises because many requests have fractional token counts from model tokenization and we historically round at the request boundary in our billing pipeline for historical consistency.
- VAT is applied to the post-rounding invoice line, so the +0.34% became ~+0.36% VAT impact on the taxable amount for the EU entity.

I've attached three files to this message. Please review the CSV and sample JSON; if BrightCart prefers we can reprocess August with ledger-level rounding for a one-off correction and issue a credit.

Attachments: usage-export-202708-tenant-brightcart.csv, reconciliation-ledger-vs-request-summary.txt, sample-requests-202708.json

From: Olivia Park <olivia@brightcart.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: BrightCart Finance <billing@brightcart.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 11:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice 2027-08-INV-4321 — reconciliation export attached

Thanks David — we reviewed the sample JSON and the CSV and can confirm the pattern you describe. Our AP would prefer the retrospective reprocessing with ledger-level rounding so the VAT base matches our internal tax filing. Can you confirm the credit and how it will show on the next invoice? Also, do you have an estimate of the timing — we need this recorded on our side before month-end closing.

If possible we'd like: (1) pro forma line showing the credit amount, (2) confirmation we'll receive a credit memo and the revised VAT calculation, and (3) the export used to calculate the credit so our auditors are happy.

Olivia

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@brightcart.com>

Date: Fri, 17 Sep 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice 2027-08-INV-4321 — confirmation of one-off ledger reprocess and credit

Hi Olivia — quick update and confirmation: we will reprocess BrightCart's August invoice using ledger-level rounding (sum fractional tokens, round once at invoice level) as a one-off adjustment. Action items and timelines:

- Ops (David) will run the reprocess and generate a credit memo by EOD Monday, 2027-09-20. The credit memo will include: the revised invoice line, the credit amount (EUR 3,196.47), and the revised VAT calculation.
- We'll attach the exact usage CSV used for the recalculation and a short reconciliation note for your auditors (same CSV format as attached earlier).
- Finance will apply the credit against the next invoice cycle and show a line item 'Ledger-level rounding credit — INV-4321'. If you prefer the credit to be issued as an immediate refund instead of offsetting next invoice, let me know and we can evaluate per your AP preference.

Neha — please confirm the VAT treatment language for the credit memo before we send to BrightCart.

Olivia — sorry for the friction here and thanks for your patience. We'll get the credit and audit artifacts to you next week.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
